en.metaDescription: Interpreter in Phuket for hospital, police and immigration. French, English and Thai with Tammy.
en.intro:
Looking for a Thai–French–English interpreter in Phuket for hospital, police, immigration or appointments? Tammy supports French and English speakers on the island.

See also hospitals in Phuket and emergency numbers.

faq.question: When should I call an interpreter in Phuket?
faq.answer: Accidents, hospitalisation, police, traffic stops, rental disputes or immigration when Thai or technical English is difficult.

faq.question: Does the interpreter cover all of Phuket?
faq.answer: Yes: Patong, Karon, Kata, Rawai, Chalong, Phuket Town and private hospitals. Contact us on WhatsApp.

faq.question: Are French, English and Thai spoken?
faq.answer: Yes: trilingual support for health professionals, authorities and local partners.

en.metaDescription: Health insurance in Phuket and Thailand: hospitalisation and French-language advice with Tammy.
en.intro:
Health insurance in Thailand is essential for expats: private hospitals in Phuket often require payment or a guarantee before care. Tammy advises in French on plans suited to your visa and profile.

Compare KrungThai AXA in Phuket or use our contact form.

faq.question: Why health insurance in Phuket?
faq.answer: Excellent private care but high costs without cover. Plans include hospitalisation, outpatient care and sometimes repatriation.

faq.question: Insurance for long-stay visas?
faq.answer: Requirements depend on visa type. A French-speaking adviser checks minimum coverage before you subscribe.

faq.question: Car and home insurance too?
faq.answer: Yes: auto, home and liability cover is available for residents in Phuket and Thailand.

faq.question: Can foreigners buy property in Phuket?
faq.answer: Rules vary for condos, villas and land. A local agent explains leasehold, company structures and foreign condo quotas.

faq.question: Popular areas?
faq.answer: Rawai, Nai Harn, Chalong, Kata, Patong; Ao Nang area in Krabi.
